subject: Hybrid hot-standby top-up and tranche conversion request
messages:
From: Rita Gomez <rita.gomez@lumahealth.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity question — sudden traffic spike

Hi Priyom,

Quick heads up — we saw a 4x spike in inference traffic for our patient-intake flow over the last 36 hours. Latency is creeping up in a few critical routes. We need a pragmatic short-term plan to avoid customer impact next week and want visibility into options to convert temporary capacity into a longer-term commit if usage sustains.

Can Redwood provide a short-term hot‑standby top‑up (preferably H100s) for 2–3 weeks and a recommended sizing/price for converting a portion to reserved capacity after the window? Also include a simple MAP and procurement steps so we can move quickly.

-Rita
Rita Gomez
Head of Product Ops, LumaHealth

From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Rita Gomez <rita.gomez@lumahealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity question — sudden traffic spike

Rita — thanks for the note and sorry about the spike. We can absolutely help. High-level options: 

1) Short-term hot‑standby pool: we can provision a 12-slot H100 burst pool (pre-warmed) for 2 weeks to absorb peak tail latencies. Estimated add: 12 H100-equivalent slots.
2) Mixed conversion: after the 2-week window we can convert up to 6 of those slots to a Reserved tranche with a discounted commit (3–12 month options) if usage justifies it.
3) Intermediate: smaller hot‑standby + request-based autoscale with routing priority for critical routes.

I attached a sizing sheet and a draft MAP with dates and simple procurement checkpoints. Can you do a 30-minute call today 2:00–2:30pm PT to walk the sizing quickly?

Best,
Priyom
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: luma_sizing_sheet_v2.xlsx, redwood_hotstandby_terms.pdf
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: david_kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity question — suggested sizing

Internal notes / quick calc: 

- Baseline: LumaHealth steady-state was ~120 qps before spike; 4x peak implies ~480 qps. Their critical route is short-context generation (~64 tokens).
- H100 slot throughput (64 tokens, average batch): ~40–50 qps per slot (conservative). Use 40 qps for headroom.
- For 480 qps -> 12 slots (480/40). Add 20% buffer for variance -> 14–15 slots.
- Recommendation: provision 15 H100-equivalent hot‑standby slots for 2 weeks. Offer conversion pricing for converting 6 slots to a 6‑month reserved tranche at 30% discount off on-demand burst rate. Remaining 9 slots remain in the hot pool for elasticity.

Operational notes for David: we should pre-warm kv-cache for the top 3 route prefixes and configure prefix caching TTL to reduce tokens generated per request by ~10% (saves token cost). Also add an autoscale fallback to a slightly cheaper A100-compatible variant if H100 capacity is constrained.

Ben — approve the conversion discount and I'll sync with pricing/legal on the tranche wording.

-Kim

From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Rita Gomez <rita.gomez@lumahealth.com>, LumaHealth Procurement <procurement@lumahealth.com>

Subject: Proposal: 15-slot H100 hot-standby + 6-slot conversion option (MAP attached)

- Provision: 15 H100-equivalent hot‑standby slots, pre-warmed, 14-day term to start 2027-06-09 00:00 PT.
- Conversion option: convert up to 6 slots into a 6‑month reserved tranche with a 30% commit discount. Conversion window: within the 14-day term.
- Pricing: hot-standby on-demand rate + 30% off for converted reserved tranche (detailed in attached pricing tab).
- Next steps (MAP):
  * 6/9: Redwood provisions 15-slot hot pool.
  * 6/10: Quick health check and perf baseline.
  * 6/18: Usage review — decision point for conversion.
  * Procurement: Luma sends PO or signature to procurement@redwood.com; we accept DocuSign or standard PO.

Attachments: luma_sizing_sheet_v2.xlsx, redwood_hotstandby_terms.pdf

If that looks good, please loop your procurement contact and we can get procurement paperwork started today.

Thanks — Priyom
